title: The Ransom of Red Chief

teacherSummary.text: Two con men, Sam (the narrator) and Bill, kidnap the son of a prominent man in Summit, Alabama, for a $2,000 ransom. The boy, calling himself Red Chief, loves the adventure and torments Bill. The father, Ebenezer Dorset, counter-offers: he will take the boy back if they pay him $250. The kidnappers pay and flee.

I read “It looked like a good thing: but wait till I tell you” slowly and put it in my own words: Sam, the narrator, says the kidnapping looked like a good idea, but we should wait until he tells us what happened. Next, craft. I notice the colon and the conversational "but wait till I tell you," as if he is leaning in to tell a joke on himself. My answer: Before the story begins, the narrator's warning tells us the kidnapping scheme failed; the fun of the story will be watching two crooks get beaten by the boy they kidnapped.
